question_text: According to the course material, the original idea for universal standards related to the treatment of prisoners was conceived by the International Penal and Penitentiary Commission, which prepared a set of rules endorsed by which body in 1934?
explanation: The original idea for universal standards for the treatment of prisoners was conceived by the International Penal and Penitentiary Commission, which prepared a set of rules endorsed by the League of Nations in 1934.

question_text: According to the course material, the Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners were approved by the Economic and Social Council in a 1957 resolution, following adoption by which body's First Congress on the Prevention of Crime and Treatment of Offenders?
option_a: The United Nations, held in Geneva in 1955
option_b: The League of Nations, held in Paris in 1934
option_c: The African Union, held in Addis Ababa in 1963
option_d: The Commonwealth of Nations, held in London in 1948
explanation: The Standard Minimum Rules were unanimously adopted by the First United Nations Congress on the Prevention of Crime and the Treatment of Offenders, held in Geneva in 1955, and approved by the Economic and Social Council in 1957.

question_text: According to the course material's summary of the Standard Minimum Rules, different categories of prisoners shall be kept in separate institutions or parts of institutions, with untried prisoners kept separate from convicted prisoners, and young prisoners kept separate from:
option_b: Only prisoners of a different nationality
option_c: Only prisoners convicted of property crimes
option_d: No one; this separation applies only to men and women
explanation: Among the separation of categories rules, young prisoners shall be kept separate from adults, alongside separating men from women, and untried prisoners from convicted prisoners.

question_text: According to the course material's discussion of the organization of treatment in prisons, two principal views exist regarding what guards should do beyond mere custody, including acting as referral agents for professional staff, and, as favored by treatment specialists in administrative roles, that guards should:
option_a: Participate more directly in treatment, dealing with inmates' minor emotional problems
option_b: Never interact with inmates under any circumstances whatsoever
option_c: Focus exclusively on physical security with no other function
option_d: Be entirely replaced by professional therapists in every single role
explanation: Two principal views on guards' roles beyond custody exist: acting as referral agents for professional staff, or, favored by treatment specialists in administrative roles, participating more directly in treatment, dealing with inmates' minor emotional problems.

question_text: According to the course material, a November 1950 survey by the American Group Psychotherapy Association's committee on group therapy and correctional agencies found that group therapy was more frequently used in training schools than in reformatories, and least frequently used in:
option_b: No institutions whatsoever, since it was universally adopted
option_c: Exclusively female institutions, with no use in male institutions
option_d: Juvenile courts, which did not use it at all
explanation: The November 1950 survey found group therapy was most frequent in training schools (21 institutions), less frequent in reformatories (13 institutions), and seldom used in prisons (5 institutions).

question_text: According to the course material, three basic approaches to group therapy literature are identified: the repressive-inspirational method, the didactic approach, and:
option_b: The purely punitive approach, with no therapeutic element
option_c: The exclusively financial approach, based on inmate wages
option_d: The approach based entirely on random chance selection
explanation: Three basic approaches to group therapy are identified: the repressive-inspirational method (emotional appeal combined with salesmanship techniques), the didactic approach (class method), and the analytic approach (free association).

question_text: According to the course material's discussion of modifying the criminal value system, this central task of penal administration requires reorganization of the formal and informal social structure of the prison so that inmates who express willingness to control their behavior according to a conventional value system:
option_b: Are immediately released from custody with no further requirement
option_c: Are punished more severely than other inmates
option_d: Are entirely isolated from all other inmates permanently
explanation: Modifying the criminal value system requires that inmates willing to adopt conventional values feel safe doing so, requiring reorganization of the prison's social structure to protect and encourage such conventionally oriented inmates.
